packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util: General-purpose helpers shipped with the API and used throughout the plugin and by client plugins: small functional-programming primitives (`La`, `La2`, `La3`), value and ordering helpers (`ComparableTuple`, `TotalOrder`), JSON and map access (`MapObject`, `JsonMapUtil`, `SpecParams`), forest/row-tree indexing (`IndexedForest`, `RowTree`), null-safe numeric and type helpers, Jira component and user lookup shortcuts, and debug/logging helpers. Most classes are static utility holders or small mutable value objects with no thread-safety guarantees unless stated.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Cal.summary: A `java.util.concurrent.Callable` whose `call()` is declared to throw one specific checked exception type `E` instead of the general `Exception`. Clients implement it (usually as a lambda) to pass code that returns a value of type `V` and may fail with `E`, for example to `JiraComponents.withThreadContextClassLoaderOf`. It has no state of its own.

members.call(): Runs the computation and returns its result (may be null if the implementation chooses). May throw the declared checked exception type `E` or any unchecked exception.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Com.summary: An immutable, totally ordered tuple of strings and numbers, used as a sort key (for example as a comparable attribute value). Instances are created only through the static `of(...)` factories; the constructor is private. Elements are compared position by position; numbers always sort before strings at the same position, and a shorter tuple that is a prefix of a longer one sorts first. Instances are immutable and safe to share between threads.

members.NIL: The empty tuple (zero elements). It sorts before every non-empty tuple, equals only other empty tuples, has hash code 0 and prints as `()`.
members.of(long): Returns a one-element tuple holding the given integer number. Never throws.
members.of(double): Returns a one-element tuple holding the given floating-point number. `NaN` and infinities are accepted; see `compareTo` for how they order.
members.of(String): Returns a one-element tuple holding the given string. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` (no message) if the string is null. The empty string is allowed.
members.of(String, String): Returns a two-element tuple (a, b). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if either argument is null.
members.of(long, long): Returns a two-element tuple of the two integer numbers, in argument order. Never throws.
members.of(String[]): Returns a tuple whose elements are the strings of the array, in order. The array is copied, so later changes to it do not affect the tuple. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the array itself is null. Null elements inside the array are not rejected here, but such a tuple will fail with `NullPointerException` (or misbehave) when compared, hashed or printed; callers must not pass null elements. An empty array yields an empty tuple equal to `NIL`.
members.of(Long[]): Returns a tuple whose elements are the given `Long` values, in order; the array is copied. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the array is null. Null elements are not checked and will cause `NullPointerException` on comparison or hashing.
members.of(String, long): Returns the two-element tuple (a, b) with a string first and a number second. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `a` is null.
members.of(String, long, String): Returns the three-element tuple (a, b, c). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if `a` or `c` is null.
members.of(java.util.List): Builds a tuple from a list of mixed values, in list order. Each element must be a `String`, a `java.lang.Number` (any subclass) or another `ComparableTuple`; a nested tuple is flattened, that is, its elements are inserted in place rather than as a single element (so `of([of(1,2), "x"])` equals the tuple (1, 2, "x")). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is null, if any element is null, or if any element has another type. An empty list yields an empty tuple.
members.compareTo(com.almworks.jira.structure.ap: Compares lexicographically. For each position up to the shorter length: two strings compare with `String.compareTo` (case-sensitive, UTF-16 code unit order); a string is greater than a number (returns 1 when this side holds the string, -1 when the other side does); two numbers are compared first by their `longValue()` (truncated toward zero) and, only if those are equal, by their `doubleValue()`. The first non-zero element result is returned, normalized to -1 or 1 for numbers (strings return the raw `String.compareTo` difference). If all shared positions are equal, the shorter tuple is smaller (-1/1), equal lengths give 0. Consequences: integer 1 and double 1.0 are equal; double 1.5 is greater than integer 1; `NaN` has long value 0, so against any number whose long value is 0 (including another NaN) the double step returns 1 in both directions; NaN is therefore not consistently ordered and should not be used. Throws `NullPointerException` if `other` is null.
members.equals(Object): True if the other object is also a `ComparableTuple` (exact class) and `compareTo` returns 0. So a tuple holding integer 2 equals a tuple holding double 2.0.
members.hashCode(): Start with 0; for each element in order, multiply the running value by 31 and add the element's hash: for a string its `String.hashCode()`, for a number the `java.lang.Double.hashCode()` of its `doubleValue()`. Integer overflow wraps silently. This keeps equal tuples (e.g. 2 and 2.0) with equal hash codes.
members.toString(): Returns the elements in parentheses separated by commas with no spaces; strings are wrapped in single quotes (no escaping), numbers use their own `toString()`. Examples: `()` for `NIL`, `('abc',5)` for of("abc", 5), `(1.5)` for of(1.5).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Con.summary: A wrapper over an SLF4J `org.slf4j.Logger` that rate-limits repeated messages per caller-chosen source key, so a recurring problem does not flood the log. For each source key, the first message is written; further messages for that key arriving within the configured interval after the last written one are dropped and counted; the next message after the interval has passed is written, preceded by a summary line saying how many were dropped. Created directly by clients with `new`. Safe for concurrent use (state is kept in a concurrent map with atomic counters; under a race two first messages for a new key may both pass).

members.<init>(org.slf4j.Logger): Creates a throttling logger writing to the given logger, with the default interval of 5 minutes. The logger must not be null (not checked; a null logger fails with `NullPointerException` when the first message is written).
members.<init>(org.slf4j.Logger, long): Creates a throttling logger with an explicit suppression interval, given in nanoseconds (as measured by `System.nanoTime()`). An interval of 0 or less effectively disables suppression only for messages that arrive at a different nanosecond timestamp; normal values are positive.
members.info(String, String): Logs `source + " " + message` at INFO level, unless an earlier message for the same source key was written less than or exactly one interval ago, in which case the message is dropped and counted. When a message for this key is written after drops, a summary line is first written of the form `<count> info log entries from <source> were not shown` (at INFO) or `<count> warnings from <source> were not shown` (at WARN); the level and wording of the summary are fixed by whichever method (info or warn) was first called for that source key, and both methods share one throttle per key. The source must not be null (`NullPointerException`). The INFO-enabled state of the logger is not consulted before throttling.
members.info(String, String, Throwable): Same as `info(String, String)` but passes the throwable to the underlying logger so its stack trace is logged with the message. Throttling and summary behaviour are identical.
members.warn(String, String): Same as `info(String, String)` but writes the message at WARN level. Shares the throttle of the same source key with `info`.
members.warn(String, String, Throwable): Same as `warn(String, String)` with the throwable attached to the logged message.
members.reset(): Forgets the throttling state of all source keys: the next message for any key is written immediately, and any counts of dropped messages are discarded without a summary line.
members.setInterval(long): Changes the suppression interval, in nanoseconds, for all source keys; takes effect for the next message. No validation.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.I18.summary: A serializable reference to a localizable message: an i18n key plus format arguments, to be resolved into text later in the viewer's locale (for example with `StructureUtil.getTextInCurrentUserLocale(I18nText)`). It is a mutable Java bean, JSON-serializable with Jackson using the properties `i18nKey` and `arguments`. Created directly by clients; not thread-safe.

members.<init>(String, Object[]): Creates a message reference with the given key (null allowed but not useful) and arguments. Each argument is normalized when stored: null stays null, any `java.lang.Number` is kept as is, and every other object is replaced by its `toString()` result; the stored array is a new array. The varargs array itself must not be null (passing a null array throws `NullPointerException`); calling with no arguments gives an empty array. This is also the Jackson creator, binding JSON properties `i18nKey` and `arguments`.
members.<init>(): Creates an empty instance with null key and null arguments, intended for bean-style frameworks; fill it with the setters.
members.getI18nKey(): Returns the i18n key of the message, possibly null.
members.setI18nKey(String): Replaces the i18n key. No validation.
members.getArguments(): Returns the stored arguments array itself (not a copy); it may be null for an instance built with the no-argument constructor. Elements are strings, numbers or null when set through the main constructor; `setArguments` may have stored anything.
members.setArguments(Object[]): Replaces the arguments array with the given array as is (no copying and no string normalization, unlike the constructor). Null is allowed.
members.equals(Object): True if the other object has exactly the same runtime class, an equal key (null equals null) and arguments arrays that are equal element by element (nested arrays compared deeply, null arrays equal only to null).
members.hashCode(): Computed in the style of Apache Commons Lang `HashCodeBuilder` with its defaults (initial 17, multiplier 37): start from 17, fold in the key's hash (0 if null), then fold in each argument's hash in order (0 for null elements; nested arrays element-wise); a null arguments array contributes a single 0 step. Consistent with `equals`.
members.toString(): If the arguments array is null or empty, returns the key alone (which can be null). Otherwise returns the key immediately followed, without any separator, by the arguments joined with commas, where null arguments become empty text; e.g. key `a.b` with arguments `x`, `1` gives `a.bx,1`. This is a debugging form, not the localized text.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Ind.summary: A read-only navigation index over a `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.Forest`, answering parent, children, sibling and subtree-end questions by row index in amortized constant time. Clients create it with `new IndexedForest(forest)`. Indexes are computed lazily on first use and cached, so the wrapped forest must not change while the index is in use (changes are not detected). Not thread-safe: even read-only queries mutate internal caches. Row positions are zero-based indices into the forest; -1 is used both as the virtual parent of top-level rows and as the 'none' result.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.f: Wraps the given forest (not copied). Reads its size immediately, so a null forest throws `NullPointerException`. No other work is done until queries are made.
members.subtreeEnd(int): Returns the index just past the last descendant of the row at `idx`, i.e. the index of the next row whose depth is less than or equal to that row's depth, or `size()` if there is none. For a leaf this is `idx + 1`. Any negative `idx` returns `size()` (the whole forest). An `idx` at or beyond `size()` fails with an index exception from the internal list.
members.parent(int): Returns the index of the parent of the row at `idx`, or -1 if that row is top-level (depth 0) or `idx` is negative. An index beyond the forest size fails with the forest's own index exception.
members.children(int): Returns an iterator over the indices of the direct children of the row at `idx`, in forest order. `idx` = -1 iterates the top-level rows. For any other out-of-range index or a row without children, returns an empty iterator. The iterator is lazy and computes siblings as it goes.
members.roots(): Returns an iterator over the indices of all top-level (depth 0) rows, in order; same as `children(-1)`. Empty for an empty forest.
members.childrenRows(int): Returns the row IDs (not indices) of the direct children of the row at `idx` (-1 for top-level rows), in order, as a new `LongList`. Returns the shared empty `LongList.EMPTY` when there are no children or the index is out of range.
members.firstChild(int): Returns the index of the first child of the row at `idx`, which is always `idx + 1` when that row is exactly one level deeper; otherwise -1. For `idx` = -1 returns 0 if the forest is non-empty, else -1. Any other out-of-range index returns -1.
members.nextSibling(int): Returns the index of the next row with the same parent as the row at `idx` (that is, `subtreeEnd(idx)` if that position exists and has the same depth), or -1 if it is the last child or `idx` is out of range (negative or at least `size()`).
members.depth(int): Returns the depth of the row at `idx` (0 for top-level rows), straight from the forest. Out-of-range indices fail as the forest's accessor does.
members.row(int): Returns the row ID at position `idx`, straight from the forest. Out-of-range indices fail as the forest's accessor does.
members.rows(com.almworks.integers.IntIterator): Returns a lazy iterator that maps each index produced by the given index iterator to the row ID at that position. The source iterator is consumed as the result is iterated.
members.size(): Returns the number of rows in the wrapped forest.
members.getForest(): Returns the forest this index was created for (the same instance).
members.root(int): Returns the index of the top-level ancestor of the row at `idx` (the row itself if it is top-level). A negative `idx` is returned unchanged.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Ind.summary: A `RowTree` that additionally keeps a lookup table from row ID to node, so nodes can be found by row ID in constant time. Row IDs must be unique within the tree. Created by clients with a constructor or with `create(Forest)`. Not thread-safe.

members.<init>(int): Creates an empty tree whose lookup table is pre-sized for about `size` rows (a capacity hint only). A negative size throws `IllegalArgumentException` from the underlying hash map.
members.<init>(): Creates an empty tree with a default capacity hint of 16.
members.create(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.f: Creates a new indexed tree and appends the whole forest under its super-root, preserving order and nesting. All row IDs in the forest are expected to be distinct.
members.createNode(long, int): Overrides the node factory: creates the node as the base class does and registers it in the row-ID lookup. A duplicate row ID is a broken invariant: with Java assertions enabled it raises `AssertionError`; otherwise the new node silently replaces the old one in the lookup.
members.forgetNode(com.almworks.jira.structure.a: Overrides the removal hook: unregisters the node and, recursively, all of its descendants from the row-ID lookup. Called by `remove`.
members.getNodeWithRowId(long): Returns the node for the given row ID. Row ID 0 returns the super-root. Returns null if no node with that ID is currently in the tree.
members.hasRow(long): True if a node with this row ID is currently registered. The super-root (ID 0) is not registered, so `hasRow(0)` is false.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Int.summary: Static helpers over the primitive collections of the `com.almworks.integers` library. Not instantiable.

members.isMutuallyExclusive(com.almworks.integer: True if the two lists have no value in common (duplicates and order do not matter); true if either list is empty. Null lists throw `NullPointerException`. The lists are not modified.
True if the two sets have no value in common; true if either set is empty. Null sets throw `NullPointerException`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Ite.summary: An immutable pair of a human-readable description of an item and an optional link to it, used for showing items in messages and UI (for example by `StructureUtil.getItemDisplayable`). Created with its constructor. Thread-safe.

members.<init>(String, String): Creates the pair. `description` is meant to be non-null (not checked at run time); `url` may be null when the item has no page to link to. The URL may be absolute or relative to the Jira base URL, depending on the producer.
members.getDescription(): Returns the display text for the item, as given to the constructor.
members.getUrl(): Returns the link to the item, or null if there is none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Ite.summary: A handle passed into callback-style iterations that lets the callback stop the iteration early. Implemented by the code running the iteration (the API's forest scanning, through the sub-interface `com.almworks.jira.structure.api.forest.raw.ForestIterationControl`); callers never create it.

members.cancel(): Asks the running iteration to stop: no further elements are visited after the current callback returns. Calling it more than once has no additional effect.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Jav.summary: A read-only `com.almworks.integers.LongList` view of a Java `java.util.List`, where each element is converted to a `long` by a given function on every access. Nothing is copied or cached, so changes to the source list are visible through the view. Created by clients with the constructor. Thread safety is that of the source list.

members.<init>(java.util.List, java.util.functio: Creates the view over `source`, converting elements with `f`. Neither argument is checked; nulls fail later on use.
members.size(): Returns the current size of the source list.
members.get(int): Returns `f` applied to the source element at `index`. An out-of-range index throws whatever the source list throws (typically `IndexOutOfBoundsException`); exceptions from `f` propagate.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Jir.summary: Static shortcuts for obtaining Jira platform services from inside a plugin, plus a helper to run code under a given thread context class loader. Every returned service is wrapped in a dynamic proxy implementing the requested interface which, for the duration of each call, switches the calling thread's context class loader to the class loader of the real service object and restores it afterwards; exceptions thrown by the service are rethrown unwrapped. Proxies for the named getters and for `getComponent`/`getComponentOfType` are cached per interface class in a static concurrent map until the cache is cleared. The class is also registered in the plugin as a component (Spring lifecycle and the API's caching-component contract) only so that the proxy cache is cleared on plugin start, stop and global cache resets. All static methods are safe to call from any thread.

members.<init>(): Public constructor used by the plugin's component container; clients have no reason to create instances, all useful methods are static.
members.getOSGiComponentInstanceOfType(Class): Looks up an OSGi service implementing the given interface (through Jira's component accessor) and returns it wrapped in a class-loader-switching proxy, or null if no such service is available. The interface class must be an interface (checked only by a Java assertion). Unlike the other getters, this result is not cached: every call creates a new proxy around the currently registered service.
members.getComponentOfType(Class): Looks up a Jira component by interface type (Jira's `getComponentOfType`) and returns it wrapped in a class-loader-switching proxy, or null if not found. The proxy is cached per interface: later calls return the same proxy (wrapping the service found the first time) until the cache is cleared. Note that this cache is shared with `getComponent` and the named getters for the same interface.
members.getComponent(Class): Looks up a Jira component by interface (Jira's `getComponent`) and returns it as a cached class-loader-switching proxy, or null if not available. Same caching as `getComponentOfType`.
members.getJiraAuthenticationContext(): Returns Jira's `JiraAuthenticationContext` (current user, locale, i18n helper), as a cached class-loader-switching proxy; null if Jira cannot provide it.
members.getProjectManager(): Returns Jira's `ProjectManager` as a cached class-loader-switching proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getProjectComponentManager(): Returns Jira's `ProjectComponentManager` (project components) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getConstantsManager(): Returns Jira's `ConstantsManager` (issue types, statuses, priorities, resolutions) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getVersionManager(): Returns Jira's `VersionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getOptionsManager(): Returns Jira's `OptionsManager` (custom field options) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getUserManager(): Returns Jira's `UserManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getGroupManager(): Returns Jira's `GroupManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getUserUtil(): Returns Jira's `UserUtil` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getPluginAccessor(): Returns the Atlassian plugin system's `PluginAccessor` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getPermissionManager(): Returns Jira's `PermissionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getApplicationProperties(): Returns Jira's `ApplicationProperties` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getIssueManager(): Returns Jira's `IssueManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getAvatarManager(): Returns Jira's `AvatarManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getComponentClassManager(): Returns Jira's `ComponentClassManager` (loads classes from plugins) as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.getGlobalPermissionManager(): Returns Jira's `GlobalPermissionManager` as a cached proxy; null if unavailable.
members.afterPropertiesSet(): Spring initialization callback: clears the static proxy cache. Final.
members.destroy(): Spring shutdown callback: clears the static proxy cache. Final.
members.clearCaches(): Clears the static proxy cache, so the next lookups wrap freshly obtained services. Called by the plugin when caches are reset.
Does nothing; there is no per-user state.
members.withThreadContextClassLoaderOf(Object, c: Runs `code` with the current thread's context class loader set to the class loader of `object` (if `object` is itself a `Class`, that class's loader; otherwise the loader of the object's runtime class; a bootstrap class gives a null loader), and returns the code's result. The previous context class loader is always restored, also when the code throws; the code's exception (of type `E` or unchecked) propagates unchanged. A null `object` throws `NullPointerException` before anything runs.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Jir.summary: A library of ready-made `La` functions (constants) that extract common properties from Jira objects (projects, issues, issue constants, versions, users, options, links) or look Jira objects up by ID, plus factories for project-permission predicates. All constants are stateless and thread-safe; unless stated otherwise each one returns null for a null argument. Lookup functions query Jira services through `JiraComponents` on every call. Some constants declare a result class (noted per constant), which is what `La.array` needs.

members.PROJECT_ID: Maps a Jira `Project` to its numeric ID. Null input gives null. Declares `Long` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.PROJECT_NAME: Maps a `Project` to its name. Null input gives null.
members.PROJECT_KEY: Maps a `Project` to its project key (e.g. `ABC`). Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.PROJECT_DESCRIPTION: Maps a `Project` to its description text (may itself be null). Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.ISSUE_ID: Maps an `Issue` to its numeric issue ID. Null input gives null.
members.KEY_PROJECT: Looks up a `Project` by project key through Jira's project manager; null if the key is null or no such project exists. Each call queries Jira.
members.ID_PROJECT: Looks up a `Project` by numeric ID through Jira's project manager; null if the ID is null or unknown.
members.ID_ISSUETYPE: Looks up an `IssueType` by its string ID through Jira's constants manager; null for a null or unknown ID.
members.ID_STATUS: Looks up a workflow `Status` by its string ID through Jira's constants manager; null for a null or unknown ID.
members.ID_PRIORITY: Looks up a `Priority` by its string ID through Jira's constants manager; null for a null or unknown ID.
members.ID_RESOLUTION: Looks up a `Resolution` by its string ID through Jira's constants manager; null for a null or unknown ID.
members.ID_COMPONENT: Looks up a project component (`ProjectComponent`) by numeric ID; null for a null ID or when Jira reports that the component does not exist (the not-found exception is swallowed).
members.ID_VERSION: Looks up a project `Version` by numeric ID through Jira's version manager; null for a null or unknown ID.
members.PROJECTROLE_ID: Maps a `ProjectRole` to its numeric ID. Null input gives null.
members.PRINCIPAL_NAME: Maps a `java.security.Principal` to its name. Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.GROUP_NAME: Maps a Crowd `Group` to its group name. Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.MODULE_COMPLETE_KEY: Maps a plugin `ModuleDescriptor` to its complete key (plugin key, colon, module key). Null input gives null.
members.LINKTYPE_ID: Maps an `IssueLinkType` to its numeric ID. Null input gives null.
members.SHAREDENTITY_ID: Maps a `SharedEntity` (filter, dashboard and the like) to its numeric ID. Null input gives null.
members.CUSTOMFIELD_TYPE: Maps a `CustomField` to its `CustomFieldType`. Null input gives null.
members.CUSTOMFIELDTYPE_KEY: Maps a `CustomFieldType` to its complete module key. Null input gives null.
members.CUSTOMFIELD_ID: Maps a `CustomField` to its string field ID (form `customfield_10000`). Null input gives null.
members.CUSTOMFIELD_LONG_ID: Maps a `CustomField` to its numeric ID (the number part of the field ID). Null input gives null.
members.FIELD_NAME: Maps any Jira `Field` to its display name. Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.ISSUETYPE_SUBTASK: Maps an `IssueType` to `Boolean.TRUE` if it is a sub-task type, otherwise `Boolean.FALSE`. Null input gives `FALSE` (never null).
members.ISSUECONSTANT_ID: Maps an `IssueConstant` (issue type, status, priority, resolution) to its string ID. Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.ISSUECONSTANT_NAME: Maps an `IssueConstant` to its untranslated name. Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.
members.ISSUECONSTANT_NAME_LOCAL: Maps an `IssueConstant` to its name translated into the current user's language (Jira's name translation). Null input gives null. Declares `String` as its result class, so `La.array` works with it.

members.<init>(): Public constructor; the class has only static methods and no state.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Jso.summary: Static helpers for validating and deep-copying JSON-compatible parameter maps, such as the parameter maps stored in specs of generators, attributes and views. A JSON-compatible value is a `String`, `Integer`, `Long`, `Double`, `Boolean`, a `java.util.List` of such values, a `java.util.Map` with `String` keys and such values, or an `org.json` `JSONArray`/`JSONObject`, which are converted to plain lists and maps on copy. Stateless and thread-safe.

members.<init>(): Public constructor; the class has only static methods.
members.copyParameters(java.util.Map, boolean, b: Deep-copies a parameter map. If `parameters` is null or empty: returns null when `allowNull` is true; otherwise returns an immutable empty map when `makeImmutable` is true, or a new mutable empty map when not. Otherwise returns the same as `mergeParameters(makeImmutable, verify, parameters)`. With `allowNull` false the result is never null.
members.mergeParameters(boolean, boolean, java.u: Merges the given maps, in argument order, into one new insertion-ordered map: entries of later maps replace values of earlier ones for equal keys (the key keeps its original position). Null maps (and a null varargs array) are skipped. Each value is deep-copied with `copyParameter(value, makeImmutable)`. If `verify` is true, every key must be a non-null `String` (otherwise `IllegalArgumentException` with message `null key` or `non-string key: <key>`) and every value must pass `checkValidParameter`. If `makeImmutable` is true the result and all nested lists and maps are unmodifiable views; otherwise all are mutable. Never returns null. Without verification, non-string keys would be cast and fail with `ClassCastException`.
members.copyParameter(Object, boolean): Deep-copies one value: `JSONArray`/`JSONObject` values are first converted with `jsonToList`/`jsonToMap`; lists become new `java.util.ArrayList`s with each element copied recursively; maps become new insertion-ordered maps whose keys are converted with `String.valueOf` and values copied recursively; any other value (including null) is returned as is. With `makeImmutable`, the new lists and maps are wrapped as unmodifiable. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if JSON conversion fails. No cycle detection (a self-containing structure overflows the stack).
members.checkValidParameter(Object): Checks that a value is JSON-compatible, recursively, and returns normally if so. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` when: the value (or any nested element) is null (`null value`); it has another type (`invalid value type: <class name>`); a nested map has a non-`String` key (`invalid map: non-string key <key>`). Errors inside containers are wrapped with context, `invalid list: invalid value at index <i>: <inner message>` or `invalid map: invalid value for key <key>: <inner message>`, with the inner exception as cause. `JSONArray`/`JSONObject` are converted and checked (so JSON nulls inside them are rejected). Excessive nesting or a cyclic structure gives `IllegalArgumentException` with message `stack overflow`. Note that `Float`, `Short`, `BigDecimal` and similar numeric types are rejected.
members.unwrapJsonCollection(Object): Converts a `JSONArray` with `jsonToList` or a `JSONObject` with `jsonToMap`; any other value (including null) is returned unchanged. A JSON parsing error is reported as `IllegalArgumentException` with message `failed to convert json object: <reason>`.
members.jsonToList(org.json.JSONArray): Marked internal. Converts a `JSONArray` to a new `java.util.ArrayList`, recursively converting nested arrays and objects; JSON null elements become Java null; other elements are kept as `org.json` returns them. Throws `org.json.JSONException` on access errors and `NullPointerException` for a null argument.
members.jsonToMap(org.json.JSONObject): Marked internal. Converts a `JSONObject` to a new `java.util.HashMap` (key order is not preserved), recursively converting nested objects and arrays; JSON null values become Java null. Throws `org.json.JSONException` on access errors and `NullPointerException` for a null argument.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La.summary: An abstract one-argument function (`T` to `R`) that also acts as a predicate, with many helpers to map, filter, collect and compare collections. It implements both `java.util.function.Function` and `java.util.function.Predicate`. Clients subclass it (usually anonymously) implementing `la`, or use the static factories. As a predicate, a result is 'truthy' when it is non-null and not equal to `Boolean.FALSE`, `Integer` 0 or `Long` 0 (so `Double` 0.0, `Short` 0 and empty strings count as true). A `La` may optionally declare its result class, needed only by `array`. Thread safety depends on the implementation; the shared constants are stateless. Helpers that build collections never modify their input.

members.<init>(): Protected constructor for subclasses that do not declare a result class (`array` will then fail).
members.<init>(Class): Protected constructor for subclasses that declare the class of their results, which `array` uses to create correctly typed arrays. Null is allowed and means 'no result class'.
members.la(Object): The function itself, implemented by subclasses: computes the result for the argument. Whether null arguments or results are allowed is up to the implementation.
members.adapt(java.util.function.Function): Wraps a standard `java.util.function.Function` as a `La` that calls it. The result has no result class. Throws `NullPointerException` if `f` is null.
members.constant(Object): Returns a function that ignores its argument and always returns `result`. For the canonical `Boolean.TRUE`/`Boolean.FALSE` instances it returns the shared constants of `constantTrue()`/`constantFalse()`; otherwise a new function without result class. Null is allowed (the function always returns null).
members.constantFalse(): Returns the shared function that always returns `Boolean.FALSE` (rejects everything as a predicate).
members.constantTrue(): Returns the shared function that always returns `Boolean.TRUE` (accepts everything).
members.isEqual(Object): Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` for arguments equal to `value` (using `value.equals(argument)`); if `value` is null, it is `TRUE` exactly for null arguments.
members.inCollection(java.util.Collection): Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` when the collection contains the argument (`Collection.contains`, live: later changes to the collection are seen). A null collection gives the constant-false function.
members.instanceOf(Class): Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` when the argument is a non-null instance of the class. A null class gives the constant-false function.
members.cast(Class): Returns a function that returns the argument cast to the class if it is an instance of it, and null otherwise (including for null). A null class gives a function that always returns null.
Returns the composition g after f: the result for x is `g.la(f.la(x))`. Null results of `f` are passed to `g` as is. The composed function takes the result class of `g`. Throws `NullPointerException` if either argument is null.
members.self(): Returns the shared identity function (returns its argument). As a predicate it accepts truthy values. No result class.
members.fromMap(java.util.Map, Class): Returns a function that looks the argument up in the map (`map.get`, live view) and returns the value, or null if absent. `rClass` becomes the declared result class (may be null). Throws `NullPointerException` if the map is null.
members.test(Object): Implementation of `java.util.function.Predicate`: same as `accepts(input)`, i.e. whether the result is truthy.
members.apply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.ut: Returns this function applied after `f`, i.e. `compose(this, f)`: for x it computes `this.la(f.la(x))`. Result class is this function's. Throws `NullPointerException` if `f` is null.
members.supply(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Returns `g` applied after this function, i.e. `compose(g, this)`: for x it computes `g.la(this.la(x))`. Result class is `g`'s. Throws `NullPointerException` if `g` is null.
members.filter(Iterable): Returns a new mutable `java.util.ArrayList` with the elements of the iterable, in order, for which this function's result is truthy. A null iterable gives an empty list.
members.filter(java.util.Iterator): Returns a lazy iterator over the elements of `iterator` that this function accepts (see `La.FilterIterator`); `remove` is not supported. A null iterator gives an empty iterator.
members.filterIterable(Iterable): Returns a lazy `Iterable` view: each call to its `iterator()` filters a fresh iterator of the source, keeping accepted elements. A null source gives an empty immutable list.
members.accepts(Object): Evaluates the function on `value` and returns whether the result is truthy: non-null and not equal to `Boolean.FALSE`, `Integer` 0 or `Long` 0. Subclasses may override it.
members.hashSet(java.util.Collection): Returns a new `java.util.HashSet` of the results of this function for each element (all results kept, including null and falsy ones; duplicates collapse). Null input gives an empty set.
members.linkedHashSet(java.util.Collection): Like `hashSet` but returns a `java.util.LinkedHashSet` keeping the order of first occurrence.
members.arrayList(Object[]): Maps each array element (varargs) through this function and returns the results in order as a new mutable list. A null or empty array gives an immutable empty list (`Collections.emptyList()`), unlike the other `arrayList` overloads.
members.arrayList(java.util.Collection): Same as `arrayList(from, true)`: a new mutable `java.util.ArrayList` with the result for every element in iteration order, null and falsy results included. Null input gives a new empty list.
members.iterable(Iterable): Returns a lazy `Iterable` whose iterators map each element of `from` through this function (see `iterator(Iterable)`). A null source gives an iterable with no elements.
members.iterator(Iterable): Returns a lazy iterator over the results of this function for the elements of `from`, computed on each `next()`. `remove()` is forwarded to the source iterator. A null source gives an empty iterator.
members.arrayList(java.util.Collection, boolean): Returns a new mutable `java.util.ArrayList` of the results of this function for each element, in iteration order. If `acceptFalsy` is false, results that are not truthy (null, `FALSE`, integer or long zero) are left out. Null input gives a new empty list.
members.arrayList(java.util.Iterator): Same as `arrayList(from, true)` for an iterator: consumes it and returns all results in a new list. Null gives a new empty list.
members.arrayList(java.util.Iterator, boolean): Consumes the iterator and returns a new list of the results, leaving out non-truthy results when `acceptFalsy` is false. Null gives a new empty list.
members.longList(java.util.Collection, com.almwo: Maps each element of the collection through `la` and returns the results that are non-null and strictly positive as a new `LongList`, in iteration order (zero, negative and null results are dropped). For a null or empty collection returns the shared `LongList.EMPTY`. A null `la` throws `NullPointerException` when the collection is non-empty.
members.intList(java.util.Collection, com.almwor: Same as `longList` for `Integer` results: returns the non-null, strictly positive values as a new `IntList`, or `IntList.EMPTY` for null or empty input.
members.addTo(java.util.Collection, java.util.Co: Adds the result of this function for each element of `from` to the collection `to`, in iteration order, skipping non-truthy results when `acceptFalsy` is false. Returns `to`. A null `from` adds nothing.
members.addTo(java.util.Iterator, java.util.Coll: Same as the collection form but consumes an iterator. A null iterator adds nothing. Returns `to`.
members.transform(java.util.Iterator): Returns a lazy iterator mapping each element of `iterator` through this function (see `La.TransformIterator`). The argument is not checked; null fails on first use.
members.transformIterable(Iterable): Returns a lazy `Iterable` whose iterators map a fresh iterator of the source through this function. A null source fails with `NullPointerException` when iterated.
members.array(java.util.Collection, boolean): Returns a new array whose component type is this function's declared result class, holding the results for the elements in iteration order; when `acceptFalsy` is false non-truthy results are dropped and the array is shortened to fit. A null collection gives an empty array. Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` if the function has no declared result class (even for null input), and `IllegalStateException` if the collection yields more elements than its `size()` reported while iterating.
For each element, computes the key with this function and puts key to the element itself into `toMap`; elements whose key is null are skipped and later elements overwrite earlier ones with the same key. Returns `toMap`. A null collection adds nothing.

For each element, computes the key with this function and the value with `valueFunction`, and puts them into `toMap`; null keys are skipped (null values are stored), later duplicates win. Returns `toMap`. A null collection adds nothing.
members.hashMap(java.util.Collection): Returns a new `java.util.HashMap` from the key computed by this function to the element, as in `mapInto` (null keys skipped, last duplicate wins).
members.hashMap(java.util.Collection, com.almwor: Returns a new `java.util.HashMap` from this function's result (key) to `valueFunction`'s result (value) for each element; null keys skipped, last duplicate wins. Null collection gives an empty map.
Like `hashMap(Collection, La)` but returns a `java.util.LinkedHashMap` keeping the order in which keys were first inserted.
members.indexOf(java.util.List, Object): Returns the index of the first list element whose result under this function equals `sample` (null matches null), or -1 if none or the list is null.
members.lastIndexOf(java.util.List, Object): Returns the index of the last list element whose result equals `sample` (null matches null), or -1 if none or the list is null.
members.find(java.util.Collection, Object): Returns the first element, in iteration order, whose result under this function equals `sample` (null matches null), or null if there is none or the collection is null or empty.
members.any(Iterable): True if this function accepts (truthy result) at least one element; stops at the first match. False for null or empty input.
members.not(): Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` exactly when this function does not accept the argument (result not truthy).
members.and(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util: Returns a predicate that is `TRUE` when both this function and `second` accept the argument; `second` is evaluated only if this one accepts. A null `second` fails only when it gets evaluated.
members.memoize(): Returns a caching wrapper: the first call for an argument computes and stores the result (null results and null arguments are cached too); later calls with an equal argument return the stored result. The cache is an unbounded plain hash map that is never cleared, and the wrapper is not thread-safe. No result class.
members.memoizeConcurrent(): Returns a thread-safe caching wrapper backed by a concurrent map. Arguments and results must not be null (null arguments or results cause `NullPointerException`, or `AssertionError` with assertions enabled). Under concurrency the delegate may run more than once for the same argument; the first stored result is kept but a racing caller may get its own computed value. Unbounded, never cleared. No result class.
members.comparator(java.util.Comparator): Returns a `java.util.Comparator` on the arguments that compares them by applying this function and comparing the results with the given comparator (see `La.LaComparator`). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the comparator is null.
members.comparator(com.almworks.jira.structure.a: Returns a comparator ordering arguments by the natural order of `function`'s results, with null results sorting first (see `La.ComparableComparator`). A null function throws `NullPointerException`.
members.liftToList(): Returns a function from an `Iterable` of inputs to the list of this function's results for its elements (in order, all results kept). A null iterable maps to null; an empty one to an immutable empty list; otherwise a new mutable list.
members.notNull(): Returns the shared predicate whose result is `TRUE` for non-null arguments and `FALSE` for null.
members.stringValue(): Returns the shared function that maps an object to its `toString()`, and null to null. Declares `String` as its result class.
Returns a function that calls `la` and substitutes `onNull` when its result is null. Takes `la`'s result class. A null `la` throws `NullPointerException` immediately.
members.image(java.util.Collection): Returns a live, read-only collection view of the truthy results of this function over `set`: iterating applies the function to each source element and skips non-truthy results; `size()` re-evaluates the function over the whole source each time. Duplicates are not removed. The iterator does not support `remove`. A null source gives an immutable empty list.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La..summary: A `java.util.Comparator` for `Comparable` values using their natural order, with null treated as smaller than any non-null value. Stateless; create with `new`.

members.compare(Comparable, Comparable): Returns 0 if both are null, -1 if only the first is null, 1 if only the second is null, otherwise `b1.compareTo(b2)`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La..summary: A lazy iterator that returns only those elements of an underlying iterator that the enclosing `La` accepts (truthy result). It is an inner class bound to its `La` instance (create with `la.new FilterIterator(it)` or via `La.filter(Iterator)`). It reads ahead one element: `hasNext()` advances the underlying iterator until it finds an accepted element. Not thread-safe.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Creates a filtering iterator over the given iterator for the enclosing `La` (the first, implicit parameter). Nothing is read until `hasNext()` or `next()` is called.
members.hasNext(): Returns whether another accepted element exists, consuming underlying elements (and evaluating the function) up to and including that element. Repeated calls without `next()` do not advance further.
members.next(): Returns the next accepted element. Throws `java.util.NoSuchElementException` if there is none.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La..summary: A `java.util.Comparator` that compares two objects by first mapping each through a `La` function and then comparing the results with another comparator. The function is evaluated on every comparison (no caching). Immutable; thread safety follows the function and comparator.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Creates the comparator. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `function is null` or `comparator is null` when the respective argument is null.
members.compare(Object, Object): Applies the function to both arguments and returns the comparator's result for the two images.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La..summary: A lazy iterator that returns the enclosing `La`'s result for each element of an underlying iterator. Inner class bound to its `La` instance (created by `La.transform` or `la.new TransformIterator(it)`). Not thread-safe.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Creates the mapping iterator for the enclosing `La` (the implicit first parameter) over the given iterator, which is not checked for null.
members.hasNext(): Returns whether the underlying iterator has more elements.
members.next(): Takes the next underlying element and returns the function's result for it (which may be null). Throws whatever the underlying iterator throws when exhausted.
members.remove(): Removes the last element from the underlying iterator, if it supports removal.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.La2.summary: An abstract two-argument function, the binary counterpart of `La`, also implementing `java.util.function.BiFunction`. Clients subclass it implementing `la(A1, A2)` or use the static helpers for currying and constant functions. Thread safety depends on the implementation.

Clients create it with `new RowTree()`; subclasses (such as `IndexedRowTree`) may hook node creation and removal. Adds a copy of the whole forest under `underNode`: the forest's top-level rows become children of `underNode`, placed right after `afterNode` (which must be a child of `underNode`) or, if `afterNode` is null, at the beginning, before any existing children. New nodes get flags 0.

General form. Copies part of `forest` into the tree: if `parentIndex` is negative, the whole forest; otherwise only the subtree below forest position `parentIndex` (its descendants, not the row itself). The copied top-level rows become children of `parentNode`, inserted right after `afterNode` (must be a child of `parentNode`) or first among its children if `afterNode` is null; deeper rows keep their relative nesting. Every created node gets `flags`. If `rowFilter` is non-null, a row for which it returns false is skipped together with its entire subtree. Returns the forest index just past the copied range (the first index after `parentIndex` whose depth is not deeper than the parent, or the forest size).
Creates a new leaf node with the given row ID and flags (through the node-creation hook) and inserts it as a child of `parentNode`: right after `afterNode` if given (it must be a child of `parentNode`), or as the first child if `afterNode` is null. Returns the new node.
members.moveNode(com.almworks.jira.structure.api: Detaches `node` (with its whole subtree) from its current place and inserts it under `parentNode`, after `afterNode` or first if `afterNode` is null. Returns `node`. Moving a node under its own descendant is not detected and corrupts the tree. Moving the super-root or a detached node throws `NullPointerException`.

members.getBooleanSystemProperty(String, boolean: Reads a JVM system property as a boolean: if the property is set, returns true only if its value is `true` ignoring case and false for any other value; if it is not set, or the key is null or empty, returns `defaultValue`.
members.lastOrZero(com.almworks.integers.LongLis: Returns the last element of the list, or 0 if the list is null or empty.
members.listsEqual(com.almworks.integers.LongLis: Compares two primitive long lists element by element, in order; null and empty lists are treated as equal to each other.

members.getDebugIssueString(Long): Returns a debug label for an issue ID: `null` for null; otherwise `(KEY ID)` if the issue's key can be looked up in Jira (e.g. `(ABC-1 10000)`), or just the ID if not. The lookup ignores permissions and swallows all errors.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.ToS.summary: Static helpers for building `toString()` texts of the form `Name{a=1,b=x}` with a `StringBuilder`: start with `begin`, add fields with `append`, finish with `end`. Stateless.

members.BEGIN: The text that opens the field list: `{`.
members.EQ: The separator between a field name and its value: `=`.
members.SEP: The separator appended after each field: `,`.
members.END: The text that closes the field list: `}`.
members.<init>(): Public constructor; the class has only static members.
members.begin(String): Returns a new builder containing the object name followed by `{` (a null name gives `null{`).
members.append(StringBuilder, String, int): Appends `name=value,` to the builder and returns the same builder.
members.append(StringBuilder, String, long): Appends `name=value,` (decimal) and returns the same builder.
members.append(StringBuilder, String, boolean): Appends `name=true,` or `name=false,` and returns the same builder.
members.append(StringBuilder, String, Object): Appends `name=`, the value's `String.valueOf` text (`null` for null), and `,`; returns the same builder.

Example: begin(`Foo`), append a=1, append b=x, end gives `Foo{a=1,b=x}`; with no fields it gives `Foo{}`. The builder is modified.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.util.Tot.summary: Defines a total order over values of arbitrary, mixed types, for sorting heterogeneous data such as attribute values. Values are first normalized: all integer-like boxed numbers (`Long`, `Integer`, `Short`, `Byte`) and floating numbers (`Double`, `Float`) become `ComparableTuple` numbers so they compare numerically with each other; strings are kept as is (strict), lower-cased (case-insensitive) or turned into `java.text.CollationKey`s (collator mode) depending on how the order was created; other objects are kept unchanged. Normalized values are wrapped (`wrap`) and compared with `COMPARATOR`. Instances are created only by the static factories and are immutable; a collator-based instance shares its collator, so thread safety then follows `java.text.Collator`.

members.COMPARATOR: A shared comparator of `TotalOrder.ValueWrapper`s. Order: a wrapper is equal to itself; wrappers holding null sort after all others (two nulls are equal). Values of the same runtime class compare by `compareTo` if they are `Comparable`, otherwise by comparing their `toString()` texts. Values of different classes are ordered by class: `ComparableTuple` (i.e. all numbers) first, then `String`, then all other classes ordered by their simple class names (`Class.getSimpleName`, case-sensitive); classes with the same simple name compare equal. Note that collation keys produced by the JDK are instances of a subclass of `java.text.CollationKey`, so in practice they fall into the 'other classes by simple name' group rather than a group of their own. Wrappers from different `TotalOrder` instances must not be mixed (checked only by Java assertions). Null wrappers are not allowed.
members.withStrictStringComparison(): Returns an order that compares strings with `String.compareTo` (case-sensitive, UTF-16 code unit order).
members.withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison(): Returns an order that compares strings after lower-casing them with the root locale. Strings differing only in case are equal.
members.withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison(java: Returns an order that compares strings after lower-casing them with the given locale (`String.toLowerCase(Locale)`); null means the root locale.
members.withCollatorStringComparison(java.util.L: Returns an order that compares strings with a new `java.text.Collator` for the locale (default strength and decomposition). A null locale throws `NullPointerException`; if no collator can be obtained, throws `IllegalArgumentException`.
Like the one-argument form but sets the collator strength (one of the `Collator` strength constants, e.g. `Collator.PRIMARY`). An invalid strength throws `IllegalArgumentException` from the JDK.
Like the two-argument form but also sets the collator decomposition mode (one of the `Collator` decomposition constants). Invalid values throw `IllegalArgumentException`.
members.withCollator(java.text.Collator): Returns an order that compares strings with the given collator, which is used as is (not copied). A null collator gives strict string comparison.
members.wrap(Object): Normalizes the value as described for the class and returns it in a new `ValueWrapper` bound to this order. Null is allowed and sorts last.
members.wrap(Object, Object): Like `wrap(Object)` but returns a `PayloadWrapper` that also carries an arbitrary payload (ignored for ordering), e.g. the row the value belongs to.
members.compare(Object, Object): Wraps both values with this order and compares them with `COMPARATOR`: negative, zero or positive as `o1` sorts before, equal to or after `o2`. For repeated comparisons, wrap once and sort the wrappers instead, since normalization (e.g. building collation keys) happens on every call.
